meta_title: KiwiDesk — tidy windows for your Mac
meta_desc: KiwiDesk keeps your Mac windows tidy automatically. No dragging, no fussing — every window lands in its place, and you stay in the calm.
mode_toggle_aria: Switch between Simple and Nerd views
mode_tooltip_simple: Curious how it works under the hood?
hero_title: Your windows, tidy — all on their own.
hero_sub: KiwiDesk arranges your open windows into a neat layout, automatically. No more dragging corners or hunting for that one hidden window. Just a calm, tidy screen.
hero_dev_kicker: A tiling window manager for macOS
quote_opening: Tiling window managers were always a nerd's toy. I set out to give anyone a calmer screen — one that just works, like magic.
quote_tagline: A window manager that works with you — not one you have to tell how to work.
quote_simple: I built KiwiDesk because I wanted to show my friends how good it feels to never tidy your windows again — calm, effortless, and honestly kind of fun.
quote_dev: Even though I'm perfectly comfortable in the terminal, I got tired of having to constantly track container nesting just to arrange my windows the way I want. KiwiDesk keeps everything flat. No unnecessary overhead, no distractions: just pure focus on my projects.
quote_byline_simple: — Maikel, planting kiwis for a calmer, happier desktop experience
quote_byline_dev_main: — Maikel, spreading kiwis (and a little more calm) wherever he can
quote_demo: Fair warning: it's about as oddly satisfying as watching kiwis stack kiwis. You'll open windows on purpose, just to watch them snap into place.
quote_cli: The day my window manager became scriptable, my desktop started running itself. I haven't dragged a window since.
quote_footer: No big company here — for now, just me and a handful of tools, each taking a tedious job off your plate so your day has more room for what you love — like eating kiwis. 🥝
quote_cta: They say an apple a day — but the kiwi's got more vitamins and bigger plans... 🥝
daily_kiwi: Now go eat a kiwi. Your vitamins will thank you. 🥝
what_body: You know the mess: a dozen windows overlapping, half of them hidden, and you spend your day nudging them around. KiwiDesk does that nudging for you. Open a window and it slots neatly into place beside the others — tidy, edge to edge, no gaps you didn’t ask for.
demo_body: Ten playful seconds with our mascot, happily arranging a screenful of windows into place — the KiwiDesk way, just with a little extra charm.
how_title: Three steps to a calmer screen.
how_body: No setup rituals, no manuals. It just starts helping.
how_1_body: Work like you always do — open apps, browse, write. Nothing new to learn.
how_2_body: Each window slides into a tidy spot automatically. Every window visible, nothing buried.
how_3_body: A tap of a key nudges the layout when you want. Otherwise, it just stays neat while you focus.
calm_before_body: Windows pile up and overlap. You drag, resize, and hunt for the one you need — again and again.
calm_after_body: Everything has a place. Your screen stays tidy on its own, so your attention stays on your work.
calm_point_1: No dragging or resizing by hand
calm_point_3: Feels native — built for macOS, top to bottom
calm_point_4: Free, and made by a small kiwi team
cta_title: Give your screen a little peace.
cta_body: KiwiDesk is on its way to the Mac App Store. Want a heads-up when it lands? It’ll be worth the wait.
feat_title: Built around one idea, done well.
feat_body: A flat, one-dimensional window model — and everything fast, scriptable, and safe that falls out of it.
feat_1_body: Every space is a flat window list. Layouts are pure functions over that array — no tree surgery, ever.
feat_2_body: bsp, stack, scrolling (PaperWM), monocle, grid, and floating. Switch between them instantly.
feat_3_body: A sandboxed Lua 5.5 VM reads ~/.config/KiwiDesk/init.lua. A broken config can’t freeze your windows — a 500 ms watchdog guards it.
feat_4_body: Script everything. Stream events to SketchyBar, JankyBorders, or your own tools over a socket.
feat_5_body: One display link per monitor, so mixed 60 / 120 Hz setups each animate at their own native cadence.
feat_6_body: User-space only. Modal keybindings run through Carbon — no Input Monitoring permission, no keylogger.
layouts_body: Every layout is a pure function over the same flat array — so switching is instant and predictable.
layout_stack: A master zone beside a stack column.
config_body: Your whole setup is one ~/.config/KiwiDesk/init.lua file — layouts, gaps, and keybindings as plain code. It runs in a sandboxed Lua 5.5 VM behind a 500 ms watchdog, so a typo can never freeze your windows.
cli_body: Every action is a command. Bind them to keys, script them, or stream live events over a Unix socket into SketchyBar, JankyBorders, or your own tools.
build_body: KiwiDesk is in CLI beta today. Clone the repo and build the release binary — packaged releases and a Homebrew cask land with 1.0.
